tool_input.command:
bd update ethos-f298 --notes "$(cat <<'EOF'
Discovered via Qodo review finding #5 on PR #532.

internal/hook/pretooluse_dispatch.go dispatchTierB (Tier B, mission-bound
spawns) writes a delegation-binding sidecar at
mission.WriteDelegationBinding (around line 879) specifically because
"additional_env from PreToolUse does NOT persist into hook script
processes" (comment on that line) -- so a Tier B worker's own subagent
tool calls can still recover delegation_id/contract_id via
ReadDelegationBinding in internal/hook/audit_log.go's fallback chain
(buildAuditEntry, ~line 230).

dispatchTierA (Tier A, no mission -- the common ad-hoc Agent() case) has
no equivalent. It allocates delegationID via mission.NewID and returns it
ONLY in its own JSON response's additional_env block (see the function
body, ~line 659-695). It never calls WriteDelegationBinding or writes any
sidecar. Since additional_env does not survive into the separately
spawned hook processes that write PostToolUse audit entries for the
subagent's own tool calls, entry.DelegationID in buildAuditEntry falls
through os.Getenv (empty), then the Tier B sidecar lookup (finds nothing,
because Tier A never wrote one), and stays "".

Confirmed empirically: PR #532's committed session audit JSONL
(.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/2026-10-12-.../audit-*.jsonl) has two Agent
spawn entries (hygiene-review, silent-failure-review -- both Tier A, no
MISSION_ID) and every subsequent Bash/tool-call entry under those
spawns carries agent_id + agent_type but delegation_id is absent on all
of them.

Fix is not a trivial copy of the Tier B sidecar: Tier B's sidecar is
keyed by session_id with a single-slot file
(sessions/<id>/delegation-binding), which is fine because mission.claim
binds one mission per session at a time. Tier A has no such
single-dispatch-per-session invariant -- the PR that surfaced this ran
TWO concurrent Tier A Agent() spawns in the same session
(hygiene-review + silent-failure-review in one response). A Tier A
sidecar keyed only by session_id would have the second spawn's write
clobber the first's, or race, and a subagent process reading it could
pick up the WRONG delegation_id -- misattributing one reviewer's tool
calls to the other reviewer's delegation record. The sidecar (or
equivalent mechanism) needs to be keyed by something the spawned
subagent process can recover on its own (e.g. passed through the
subagent's actual env rather than Claude Code's additional_env, or
keyed by a value derivable from the agent_id Claude Code does pass
through -- worth checking whether agent_id survives into the subagent's
real process env already, since audit_log.go reads it successfully from
input["agent_id"]).

Design/implement under docs/audited-delegation.md -- amend that spec
with the Tier A binding mechanism in the same PR per this repo's own
CLAUDE.md rule on internal/mission lifecycle docs, even though this
lives in internal/hook: the feature DES-054 and its doc both call this
"every Agent tool call is now bound to a delegation record," which Tier
A is not actually achieving for the subagent's own subsequent calls.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -5

tool_input.body:
Finding #5 ("Spawned reviews lose traceability") is confirmed valid and is a real, pre-existing hook defect — not something I'm fixing in this PR.

Traced it: `dispatchTierB` (`internal/hook/pretooluse_dispatch.go:~879`) writes a delegation-binding sidecar explicitly because `additional_env` from PreToolUse doesn't persist into the separately-spawned hook processes that write PostToolUse audit entries (see the comment at that line). `dispatchTierA` — the ad-hoc `Agent()` path, no mission, the common case — has no equivalent. It allocates `delegationID` and returns it only in its own JSON `additional_env`, which never reaches the subagent's own subsequent tool-call audit entries. `buildAuditEntry`'s fallback chain in `internal/hook/audit_log.go` then finds nothing for Tier A, and `delegation_id` is silently blank on every one of those entries.

Confirmed empirically against this PR's own committed audit log: the two `hygiene-review`/`silent-failure-review` `Agent` spawns (both Tier A) have every downstream tool call tagged with `agent_id`/`agent_type` but no `delegation_id`.

Not a one-line fix: a naive copy of the Tier B single-slot sidecar (keyed by `session_id`) would misattribute delegation IDs the moment two Tier A agents run concurrently in one session — which this PR's own session did. Filed as `ethos-f298` with the concurrency hazard and a design note pointing at `docs/audited-delegation.md` for the amendment. Out of scope for a repo-hygiene PR; tracking separately rather than expanding this one.
